claims.statement: The pinned fragment states that Codespaces charges use monthly billing even for an otherwise annually billed account. This snapshot billing statement does not verify an account invoice or authorize spending.

Organization Codespaces policies apply only to codespaces paid for by that organization; a personally funded codespace from an organization repository is not bound by these policies. Repository membership alone therefore does not establish policy coverage. The payer/ownership article remains separate evidence; no actual effective policy or payer was observed.

The policy-creation fragment selects Codespaces policies through an included navigation reusable, starts Create Policy and names the policy. This partial procedure is not completed constraint configuration, activation or authorization; include resolution and effective behavior remain separate.

Codespaces policy targeting defaults to all repositories and can otherwise select repositories through the described UI. An existing policy containing Maximum codespaces per user cannot be narrowed to selected repositories because that constraint is organization-wide. Preserve this constraint-specific exception rather than assuming all targeting is independently granular. Captions were read, not screenshot pixels or actual effective targets.

Spending limits may prevent new codespaces or opening existing ones when billable costs would occur for a personal, organization or enterprise account. The source advises checking budgets for usage suitability and links budget setup; this is not approval to raise limits, bypass restrictions or access financial settings.

The pinned note excludes repositories owned by managed user accounts from Codespaces availability and links the enterprise-managed-user explanation. Do not broaden the exclusion into all organization-owned repositories or infer current account eligibility from this fragment.

The dev-container command-palette example creates a new configuration, then explicitly overwrites an existing file in its template-specific context before showing all definitions. This example is not blanket authority to overwrite user configuration or proof that the new configuration is safe or valid. Captions and context were read; no commands, overwrite or installation performed.

The fragment supplies platform-specific editor command-palette shortcuts for Mac and Windows/Linux. This UI navigation step alone grants no command execution, administrative permission or configuration mutation.
